title: 50% Cheaper than Specialized? The First US-Designed Chinese Gravel Bike

takeaways.text: Clearance is 55 mm (it ships with 45 mm tires); geometry is conventional, short and tall endurance gravel with a 70 mm bottom-bracket drop that made fast loose corners harder work.
The frame is notably compliant on gravel at low pressure; the seat-cluster junction looks like a compliance feature but he was told it is mostly aesthetic.
US$3,200 with electronic shifting, carbon wheels, seatpost and cockpit, UDH, in-frame storage and a power meter; 19.44 lb (about 8.8 kg) without pedals.
A size-M comes with a sensible 39 cm bar, threaded bottom bracket and fully internal routing with an optional external head-tube port; there is no frameset-only option.
Against dual-sided Garmin pedals the XDS crank power meter read about 8–10 W high but tracked changes consistently.

disclosure: The review bike was collected from a new XDS dealer in Portland; no payment is stated.
summary: A US gravel ride review of the X-LAB GT8 with Shimano GRX Di2, compared with a Specialized Diverge and Santa Cruz Stigmata.
